# LEDGER — MVS "My Vampire System" · v1 (auto-harvested from source · blueprint v3)

*First ledger for this show. Source: operator-supplied `MVS 1100.md`, harvested **eps 1–50** ("Just an Old Book" → "VR Game") in five bands. Generated by the harvest pass against Blueprint v3. All rows status **CANON** — every quote is source-verbatim, with source typos and grammar preserved (punch-up is W3's job). Cross-checked against `world_mvs.md` HARD BLOCKS; collisions are flagged in §5 and §7, not silently resolved.*

*Provenance warning, up front: four rows in Blueprint v3 are attributed to MVS and **do not exist anywhere in eps 1–50** — slot 21's "Mr Talen, I'm sorry. I didn't realize." and Brennan's "Mr. Quinn Talen. What… what can I do for you?"; slot 22's "Don't ever reveal your secret to anybody, son… promise me you will do everything it takes."; slot 15's "thirty days to reach level three, otherwise you'll be expelled." The slot-22 line **contradicts canon** (Ep 1: the parents die off-page in the war, the book is delivered by a government agent, and Quinn never knew their faces). Treat all four as prior-promo invention until proven from a later band. See F-105.*

---

## 1. THE MASTER ARC REPORT

**PUBLIC PRICING — PRESENT, continuous, and the strongest in the catalog. Device variant, worn on the body.**

MVS does not have a pricing ceremony; it has a **pricing instrument strapped to the wrist and never removed.** The authority installs it in Ep 3 and names it in the same breath as a kindness: *"Placed on your wrist is your lifeline… When not in use, the wristwatch will display a number - Your corresponding power level,"* (Griff, Ep 3). The formal rite (the level test, Eps 5–6) is the *installation*, not the humiliation — it happens in an empty wasteland with four peers and no crowd, and returns *"Quinn Talen, your overall current power level is that of a level 1 ability user,"* (Jane, Ep 6).

The humiliation is that **every stranger re-runs the test for free, in one glance, forever.** The instrument is quoted being read off his body across all five bands: *"The first place the student's eyes went to was of course Quinn's watch. Seeing the low number his confidence grew."* (Ep 10) · *"Seeing the number 1 shine brightly on it"* (Ep 19) · *"the boy spotted his attacker's glowing wristwatch, which lit up brightly in the dark, displayed the number one"* (Ep 17) · *"No ability, power level 1." The watch said again.* (Ep 30) · *"Each of them had a power level 2 displayed on the watches."* (Ep 43).

**Two structural findings that override the blueprint's default staging:**

1. **The register is contempt, not laughter.** In 50 episodes there is no laughing-square beat aimed at Quinn. The room's verdict is *dismissal* — *"After watching the fight, many of the students were quite disappointed."* (Ep 32); *"but you will always be a weak level one."* (Momo, Ep 43). Do not import a laughing-crowd staging from the WBT/Flameborne lane. It is not in this source, and forcing it produces a wrong-show alarm.
2. **RE-PRICING — ABSENT IN PUBLIC ACROSS ALL FIVE BANDS, and canon-blocked from ever arriving.** HARD BLOCK 2 pins the watch at Level 1 permanently; it reads mutant-cell count and cannot read vampire MC. **MVS is a show whose pricing instrument is architecturally incapable of re-pricing its hero.** This is not a thin slot. It is the design.

**What the source gives instead — four usable substitutes, in ascending order of strength:**

- **The private verdict against the public one.** The show's whole irony engine is two screens in one frame: the watch face reading `1` where everyone can see it, and the System reading `< Congratulations you are now Level 3>` (Ep 30) where only Quinn and the audience can. Ep 30 stages both **one page apart**.
- **The true measurement spoken publicly and thrown away.** Leo, mid-spar, in a full weapons hall: *"About level 14 or 13 maybe, that's pretty good for a first-year student."* (Ep 32). The crowd reads the fight as a teacher toying with a runt and leaves disappointed. **A real re-measurement that the public refuses to register** — the single most transplantable asset in the harvest.
- **The proof seen by a hundred people and named by nobody.** The beast stone in Quinn's hand: *"The black ball started to glow, it glowed brighter than any of the balls the other students had held before."* (Ep 43). Momo registers it privately — *"How is that possible, he was able to activate the basic tier weapon fully?"* — then re-prices him **down**, out loud, seconds later.
- **The drop that lands on a wrong reading.** Loop bows in a locked empty classroom (Ep 37) and keeps a secret he has misidentified: *"I don't know why you're hiding behind that fake power level of yours"* (Ep 38). Deference, privately, from a boy who thinks he is sparing himself a murderer.

**Ruling for W2/W3: build the promo arc PRICING → PRIVATE RE-PRICING → THE CONCEALMENT TAX.** The payoff exists, the audience gets it, and it is paid for in silence — which is resolution-withholding native to the show rather than imposed on it. The promo must **never** end on a public reveal or a moving number. The loaded gun is Ep 43: the whole hall watching the stone glow and the world declining to read it.

## 4. HARVEST — EXCHANGE SHAPES

**a) The volunteer inversion** (Eps 42–43) — flag KEEP-VERBATIM. **The single strongest shape in the harvest.**
Tyrant calls for a volunteer to stone the hero's friend → total silence → the weakest boy in the room volunteers, *smiling*: "Pick me! I don't mind having a little try." → he states his reason to the hall: "Why do we have these powers… Isn't it to protect ourselves, to fight those who harm our friends and family." → "I have taken a beating my whole life and I was weak back then, what do I care if I take another beating now." → the throw, and the aim is wrong on purpose: "it landed straight in the student's stomach standing by the side of the board." → "What the hell are you guys doing standing there, get him!"
*(ACT→PUNISHMENT with the act unmistakable on first hearing, and the punisher able to cite it. Textbook.)*

**b) The keeper's bargain** (Eps 22–23) — flag KEEP-VERBATIM. *(New shape candidate — the secret-identity lane's counterpart to the poisoned offer.)*
"What happened at the library, what did you do?" → stonewall: "Why bother asking if you already know what happened?" → the witness names it: "You're a Vampire, aren't you?" → refusal: "I'm not a vampire, I became like this from an Ability book." → **her counter-terms**: "Fine, I will keep this as a secret but only on one condition." → "If you need to feast on someone, then feast on me." → "It's a deal," Quinn said as the two of them shook hands.
*(The blackmail scene that turns into devotion — more disturbing than extortion would have been.)*

**c) The wrong-explanation pile-on** (Ep 30) — flag KEEP-VERBATIM. Near-identical to the blueprint's canonical shape, source-verbatim.
A bare fist slices a beast weapon in half → Brandon: "What the, my weapon, it's faulty!" → the room adopts it: "Brandon obviously was using a faulty weapon." → escalation: "Unless, it has to be it, he cheated and used an ability." → the authority's flat refusal: "And I'm telling you now, Quinn didn't use a single ability." → the witness discredited: "He's blind?"

**d) The accidental-truth laugh-off** (Ep 9) — flag KEEP-VERBATIM. **The most MVS-native shape in the source.**
The disguised confession: "Have you ever heard of an ability that is weaker in sunlight?" → the laugh: "What are you, crazy? I've never heard of something like that." → the world-law recited: "Abilities are something our bodies learn." → the punchline that is the answer: "Are you sure, you have not accidentally grabbed a fantasy book about vampires?" → the tax paid in silence — he lets it go.

**e) The apology ladder → the flipped cliff** (Ep 37) — flag KEEP-VERBATIM. *(The recognition drop, private, ending on the hero's ignorance.)*
Loop, bowing: "I'm sorry about yesterday," → "I Promise I won't tell anyone about your secret, please whatever you do just let me live." → Quinn, bluffing blind: "Thanks for keeping my secret, besides I don't really have a grudge against you." → Loop: "Thank you, thank you for sparing me," → "I just don't want what happened to Brandon happening to me." → Quinn: "Brandon?" … "What happened to Brandon?"
*(The deference ladder climbs three rungs, then the last rung breaks under the hero — he is being thanked for a murder he hasn't heard about.)*

**f) The forced-participation ladder** (Ep 42) — flag KEEP-VERBATIM.
Order → refusal → the refuser punished → next → compliance → the compliant one *praised*: "Alright then, you the girl with the brown hair, you go first." → "I… I can't," → "Really, well if you can't then we have no choice," → the ball into her stomach → "Get her out of here," Momo said. "Next!" → the next boy throws, Vorden coughs blood → "You see that, now that was perfect, that is exactly how everyone should throw the ball."

**g) The half-conversation overheard** (Ep 24) — flag KEEP-VERBATIM. *(New shape candidate — cheap in audio, extremely legible on first hearing.)*
Peter rounds a corner → one voice, alone: "Would you two calm down," → **pause where the reply should be** → "I don't care if he hurt the little one's feelings…" → **pause** → "Look, if you get involved and hurt them, I won't forgive you. I won't let something like last time happen again." → Peter peeks: "still the only person he could see was Vorden."
*(The absent second voice does the entire dramatic job. Executes HARD BLOCK 6 perfectly — never named, never explained.)*

**h) The alibi-of-contempt** (Ep 41) — flag KEEP-VERBATIM. *(New shape candidate; not in the blueprint index.)*
The hero is acquitted by the world's low opinion of him. The instrument works; the *interpretation* saves him. "Now tell me, did you kill Brandon Richardson last night?" → "No, I did not." → "He's telling the truth." → "I mean how would it even be possible, he's only a level one." → "It looks like we no longer have any leads."

**i) The apologetic-extortion ladder** (Ep 15) — flag KEEP-VERBATIM.
"Lucky us, to meet some of the few level 1s in this whole school. Hand over ten credits each and we'll let you head inside." → "But that's all the credits we have." → "Look I don't want to do this, but if I don't then my arse gets beat… Hand over the credits, now!" → the wrists touch, the credits move.
*(The pricing collected by someone who is himself priced.)*

**j) The reversible-torture loop** (Ep 49) — flag KEEP-VERBATIM. *(New shape candidate — healing as the torturer's tool.)*
"Just nod if you agree." → [Peter shakes his head] → fingers broken one by one → "all five of Peter's fingers had broken and Peter still hadn't agreed" → "Hey Jerry, get over here." / "Do your thing Jerry." → the bones re-form → "He grabbed Peter's fingers again and repeated the process again and again." → "Good, see, now if you had done that in the first place, we wouldn't have had to go through all that."

**k) The kindness that triggers the bite** (Ep 19) — flag KEEP-VERBATIM.
The last useless book closes → Layla is standing there → "Are you okay?" → hand on the forehead → "You're so cold? Do you want me to take you to the nurse's office?" → "Quinn hadn't heard a single word she had said." → "A weak sorry escaped his lips… as he bit into her neck."
*(The only person who offers help becomes the meal. Four turns, zero villain.)*

## 5. THE THIN-SLOT REPORT (authorship map)

- **PUBLIC RE-PRICING — canon-BLOCKED, not thin.** HARD BLOCK 2 pins the watch at Level 1 forever. No skeleton may stage "the number jumps and the room goes silent." Substitutes are ranked in §1; the Ep 43 glowing stone is the best.
- **SLOT 21 — RECOGNITION DROP: EMPTY for Quinn across 50 episodes.** Nobody ever defers to him for who he is. The mechanic demonstrably works in this world — it fires for Vorden's displayed 5 (Ep 19, *and it's a bluff*), for Leo's war name (Ep 30), for Fay's rank (Ep 47) — which makes the withholding pointed. **Stage the drop as withheld promise, never as event.** Loop's private bow (Ep 37) is the only version the show permits, and it rests on a wrong reading.
- **SLOT 22 — DEATHBED CHARGE: EMPTY, and canon-contradicted.** No parent speaks in eps 1–50. The parents die off-page in the war; the book arrives via a government agent; *"he grew up not knowing what his parents looked like"* (Ep 1). The recorded-elder variant (Eps 39–40) is the honest substitute — a message left for a stranger by someone probably long dead. **The blueprint's MVS-attributed line "Don't ever reveal your secret to anybody, son…" is not canon here and collides with Ep 1.**
- **SLOT 3 — SACRIFICE LINE: EMPTY as scene, narrated-only as fact.** No family gift, no hoarded cost, nothing weaponized by a villain, nobody ever mentions his parents to his face in 50 episodes. The functional substitute the source does supply is friend-sacrifice: Vorden's ten credits (Ep 16), Layla's standing blood offer (Eps 23, 46), Peter's five fingers (Ep 49). W3 authors or transplants.
- **SLOT 8 — ALL-IN WAGER: no public stakes-both-sides anywhere in 50 eps.** The closest is Momo's *no-win* wager (Ep 45) — both outcomes named, both punish — which is arguably a better fit for this show than a symmetrical bet. The Layla bargain (Ep 23) has terms and a handshake but no audience and no death on the table.
- **SLOT 19 — OVERHEARD VERDICT: runs INVERTED, and this is an asset, not a defect.** MVS's hero carries almost no overheard truth; the **audience** carries it. Duke's "our little secret" (Ep 47) and the leaders' meeting (Ep 48) are given straight to the listener — Quinn will never learn a General ordered the torture. Stage as dramatic irony, or re-stage as a physical overhear.
- **SLOT 10 — WITNESS LINE: thin by design through Ep 21.** Layla sees everything and says nothing aloud for ten episodes; every early witness beat is interior. The slot opens at Ep 22 and is well-stocked after.
- **IMAGE CLASS H — DESTROYED TOKEN: no canonical instance.** No bully destroys the hero's love-object in public. Every candidate is self-inflicted (the glasses, Ep 1) or displaced onto Peter (Ep 49). Ask the operator before staging class H.
- **The register warning, restated because it will be the most common wrong-show error:** MVS prices with **contempt and dismissal**, never with laughter. There is no laughing square in this source.
- **Structural:** build **PRICING → PRIVATE RE-PRICING → THE CONCEALMENT TAX**, which the source supports verbatim end to end, and which satisfies resolution withholding by canon rather than by restraint.

## 6. FREE HARVEST (≤10)

1. **"Let's see how long you can survive in this cruel world, Quinn,"** (unnamed superior, Ep 6) — an unseen man in a chair, on a file, alone. The show's real danger (HARD BLOCK 3) in nine words, better than any villain line in the source.
2. **"Evolution? What the fuck!"** (Quinn, Ep 17) — canon profanity landing exactly where the audience is. The reaction shot of the entire premise.
3. **"I want you to make me a Vampire."** (Layla, Ep 22) — the reveal scene's payoff is not a threat but a fan request. Funny and unsettling in the same breath.
4. **"I don't know whether it's a good thing or a bad thing that I'm finding it easier every time I do this."** (Quinn, Ep 36) — said with a boy's face inches from his own. The moral spine of the run.
5. **"What a waste."** (Quinn, Ep 30) — three words over a bleeding classmate, showing the System eating his moral floor with no horror-narration at all.
6. **"Of course, as long as no one finds out about our little secret," Duke said with a smile.** (Ep 47) — retroactively recontextualises the whole assembly-hall sequence. The bully was doing homework for a General.
7. **"Since when has this world ever been fair? Blame the people at the top for not looking out for us."** (Rylee, Ep 26) — the injustice engine handed to a low-level bully who is right about the diagnosis and wrong about the treatment.
8. **"Another one?" Hayley sighed** (Ep 20) — two words that build an institution processing damaged children on a conveyor belt.
9. **"Each one of them was dealing with their own problems, yet not one of them knew of the others."** (narrated, Ep 37 — REVOICE) — three boys, three secrets, one dorm room, lights out.
10. **"It's best to ask your students to pack some sun cream and their sunglasses"** (Nathan, Ep 48) — a death sentence for a Halfling, delivered as a packing list. Best cliff-forward in the harvest.

**Two dating corrections for `world_mvs.md`:**
1. **Leo's aura-read of Quinn is dated ~Ep 95 in Layer 2. It actually opens at Ep 30** — "it reminded him of an aura of that of the beasts or the Dalki had, one that wasn't human" → "Hmm, just what are you hiding Quinn?" The suspicion loop is available *inside the entry window*, 65 episodes earlier than the file says, and is materially cheaper to promo.
2. **The entry map dates the assembly-hall torture at ~Ep 44.** There is an earlier assembly-hall beating of Vorden by second-years at **Ep 21**, with the crowd frame-up attached. Either two incidents exist or the Ep 44 dating covers only the second — operator ruling needed before any promo cites "the assembly hall."

**Prior-promo provenance flag:** Eps 28–30 is plainly the source behind the shipped **"Weapon Selection"** promo cited in Blueprint v3. The source names **Loop** as Brandon's friend in the crowd, not the defeated opponent — the promo swapped them. Do not count that band as fresh territory without checking against the shipped asset.

**Source-error inventory (harvested as-is; know they're errors):** Rylee's Inspect reads **"Rylee Blade"** (Ep 17), the same surname as **Vorden Blade** — almost certainly a slip; quoting the full name would imply a family link that is not canon.
